title: Post-Apocalyptic Train Station
description: This is a personal 3D environment project showcasing my end-to-end workflow. I was responsible for all aspects of the scene's creation, including modeling, texturing, shading, and lighting, to bring this forgotten and atmospheric space to life.

body.text: To establish the visual foundation for this project, I spent time on Google and ArtStation collecting references for overgrown foliage, weathered textures, and abandoned structures. To bridge the gap between real-world references and my imagination, I used generative AI to create targeted concept images for the abandoned tram and the broader station layout. This hybrid approach to reference gathering perfectly set the tone and color palette for the entire project.

Placing the foliage efficiently while maintaining a highly organic feel was a key focus. I combined procedural and manual techniques by building a custom Houdini tool to scatter the base layer of vegetation. I then refined the scene by hand using the UE5 foliage brush, allowing me to perfectly art-direct the specific placement and final aesthetic.

title: Dragon Kisser
description: This is a student capstone project successfully published on Steam. I worked on this project as an Environment Artist Lead who actively communicated with environment, art, and programming teams to balance visual quality with technical efficiency. I collaborated on creating medieval Spanish village surrounding the arena and was solely responsible for the rhythm-minigame background environment. I used Maya and ZBrush for modeling, Substance Painter and Substance Designer for texturing, Unreal Engine 5 as the game engine, and Perforce for version control.

body.text: To populate the environment and give the architecture character, I modeled decorative props, such as lanterns, planters, and chimneys. Because these props were instanced throughout the environment, I kept their polygon counts low while preserving their overall shapes.
I also setup the house Blueprints so that we can easily customize houses with exposed parameters for selecting prop models.

I created brick and stucco texture sets using Substance Designer for the mask-driven material used on house walls. I also made a trim sheet for the remaining architectural components. We ended up using two materials to shade all the house assets: the wall-blending material and the material using the trim sheet.

I made one master material for houses that uses in-engine masking, which enables us to paint a mask while in Mesh Paint Mode. By doing so, brick and stucco materials could blend naturally in the engine and we could change the stucco coverage over bricks inside Unreal instead of authoring a new texture variation for each house in Substance Painter.

I set up master materials that are reusable for all small props. I showed environment artists how to assign their textures in the material instance's parameter panel and create simple variations by adjusting parameters.

I was fully responsible for the minigame environment, handling its development from overall spatial layout to final scene assembly. I modeled the central stage asset by interpreting concept art from our Art Director, ensuring strong fidelity to the visual direction.

title: Wooden Crate
description: A material and look development study focused on realistic surface detailing and weathered wood response. Working with a provided base model, I was responsible for retopology, UV editing, texturing, shader setup, lighting, and rendering in Houdini using RenderMan.
